elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered (b): "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED..." — the prior Licensor-only formulation is replaced with "EITHER PARTY'S", and the added carve-out sentence is likewise bilateral ("EACH PARTY'S LIABILITY").

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap reads "THE FEES PAID BY THE LICENSEE ... IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — it uses "paid" only (not "paid or payable") and contains no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section (a) is untouched and remains one-directional: "IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE TO LICENSEE OR TO ANY THIRD PARTY FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES". Licensee (our client) receives no reciprocal exclusion, so it remains exposed to Licensor's consequential-damages claims.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "THE CAP IN SECTION (b) SHALL NOT APPLY TO, AND EACH PARTY'S LIABILITY SHALL BE UNCAPPED FOR, ... ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS...".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out list covers only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered text.
Added sentence expressly excepts "ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" from the Section (b) cap for each party, addressing the Article XII Licensee indemnity.
Added sentence: "...ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT."
Added sentence: "...ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT."
No fraud carve-out in the added sentence or elsewhere in Article XIII.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out was added; worse, retained (a) still states "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY ... MAY RESULT IN ANY INFRINGEMENT ... OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ... RIGHTS OF ANY PERSON".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that Licensee's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" for cap purposes; the newly mutual cap in (b) could therefore be read to cap Licensee's payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Operative (b) now runs to "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY"; the deterministic check confirms no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "EXCEED THE FEES PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" replaces the illusory "ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID" basis; "fees" is used in its ordinary sense (no narrow defined term in this Agreement).
Added sentence carves "ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" out of the Section (b) cap for each party.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added sentence carves out "ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS".
Added sentence carves out "ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the cap in (b) is now bilateral and set at fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, and a single appended sentence lifts indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct out of the cap for each party.

Preferred level fails on five points the drafter should note if pushing higher: no "paid or payable" wording, no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, no data-protection/security, fraud or IP-infringement carve-outs, and no statement that Licensee's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

The rationale's justification for leaving Section (a) alone is wrong on the facts: "IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE ... FOR ANY SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" protects the Vendor only and leaves Licensee exposed to consequential-damages claims; the asymmetry is adverse, not favourable. This does not defeat the fallback (which omits the exclusion element), but the comment should not assert a Customer benefit that does not exist.

Retained (a) still absolutely excludes Licensor liability for IP-infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology, which sits directly against the preferred IP carve-out; flag it if the preferred position is pursued.

Because the cap is now mutual with no payment carve-out, consider adding "Licensee's obligation to pay fees due hereunder is not subject to this cap" only if pursuing preferred — it is outside the fallback checklist and its omission is correctly not treated as a defect here.

Minimality holds: two surgical operations, no survival tail, no added procedures, no deletion of favourable retained language ((c) and the (a) exclusion remain intact), and the carve-out list matches the fallback checklist exactly.
Intent is preserved: the added sentence cross-refers to an existing "SECTION (b)", introduces no undefined terms, and does not contradict the retained material-inducement statement in (c).
